text:
kai: Quick note — new onboarding run leaked emails and some req_ids were missing when users flip OTEL ordering. Repro in `samples/onboard-simple`.

marisol: Can you paste the snippet and how you ran it?

kai: Repro: `git checkout samples/onboard-simple && REDWOOD_LOG_LEVEL=debug TELEMETRY_HOOK_ORDER=otel_first ./dev up`. Snip: 
```
2026-04-10T10:02:11.100Z DEBUG http.core request -> POST /v1/complete
2026-04-10T10:02:11.101Z DEBUG http.core raw-headers: Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED user=pat@example.com
2026-04-10T10:02:11.102Z WARN telemetry req_id missing for outbound request
```

marisol: Looks like two things: (1) OTEL-first makes our logging hook run later so some libs log without req_id, (2) our header sanitizers catch Authorization but not key=value style `user=` headers.

kai: I tried `REDWOOD_LOG_LEVEL=info` and it hides most noise but we still need to avoid any PII in debug paths.

marisol: Action items: bump sample SDK to a stable 0.9.x release so hook ordering is consistent, add a conservative `normalizeHeaders()` in our lowest-level fetch wrapper that runs before any call to node internals, and add a CI logs-scan job that fails if lines match common PII regexes (emails, ssn). Also document `TELEMETRY_HOOK_ORDER` behavior in quickstart.

sdk-bot: Related SDK PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/440 (header normalization + hook docs)

qa-bot: Suggest adding an integration that runs sample with both `TELEMETRY_HOOK_ORDER=otel_first` and `logging_first` and asserts every debug line contains either `req_id=` or `trace_id=`.

kai: Agree. I'll open a small PR to add the scrub and a README blurb: "If debug network logs appear without req_id or contain PII, set REDWOOD_LOG_LEVEL=info and upgrade the sample SDK."

marisol: Prefer landing the scrub behind `REDWOOD_SCRUB_STRICT=false` default, then enable in canary for a week. Keep the scrub conservative to avoid redacting useful non-PII tags.

kai: Will do. Leaving my dev instance running to validate once CI green. Thanks :thumbsup:
